reason: The cited evidence does not provide specific data for HfNbTaTiZr; E4 shows comparable lattice/electronic behavior in other concentrated alloys, but the quantitative predictions (4–7 W/(K·m), 10–17 W/(K·m), 30% improvement) are unsupported by the passages, and E1/E2 discuss lattice distortion effects without linking them to thermal transport in this alloy.
premises: Lattice thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr is nearly constant (4–7 W/(K·m)) below 200 K.
Electronic thermal conductivity dominates above ~300 K.
Total thermal conductivity is 10–17 W/(K·m) at 300–1200 K for oxygen-free samples.
A new model decoupling lattice and electronic transport will improve accuracy by ~30% over Debye-based approaches.
Local lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations are the key structural mediators.
